glosses: Control or occupancy of something for which one does not necessarily have private property rights.

examples.text: Once complete, guide rails will be installed inside the tunnels ready for the box jack itself - which NR intends to push into place during a nine-day engineering possession in September, following a trial push in late August. [...] A small number of weekday and weekend possessions will also be required on June 20-21, September 5-6, and between December 19-March 2021, [...]

glosses: Something that is owned.

examples.text: The car quickly became his most prized possession.
I would gladly give all of my worldly possessions just to be able to do that.

glosses: Ownership; taking, holding, keeping something as one's own.

examples.text: The car is in my possession.
I'm in possession of the car.

glosses: A territory under the rule of another country.

examples.text: Réunion is the largest of France's overseas possessions.

glosses: The condition or affliction of being possessed by a demon or other supernatural entity.

examples.text: Back then, people with psychiatric disorders were sometimes thought to be victims of demonic possession.
How long hath this possession held the man?

glosses: The condition of being under the control of strong emotion or madness.
Control of the ball; the opportunity to be on the offensive.

examples.text: The scoreboard shows a little football symbol next to the name of the team that has possession.
Their first half was marred by the entire side playing too deep, completely unable to build up any form of decent possession once the ball left their bewildered defence.

glosses: A disposal of the ball during a game, i.e. a kick or a handball.

examples.text:
2019 In the mix: Who's pushing for selection for round eight? Australian Football League, 7 May 2019. Accessed 7 May 2019.
Defender Colin O'Riordan had 41 possessions in the NEAFL last week to continue his outstanding form, while Ryan Clarke had 47 in the Swans' big loss to Brisbane.

glosses: A syntactic relationship between two nouns or nominals that may be used to indicate ownership.

examples.text: Some languages distinguish between a construction like 'my car', which shows alienable possession — the car could become someone else's — and one like 'my foot', which has inalienable possession — my foot will always be mine.

glosses: To invest with property.

translations.source_sense_description: Erregungszustand, der als „Inbesitznahme“ der Person durch eine übernatürliche Kraft gedeutet wird

glosses: Jouissance, faculté actuelle de disposer ou de jouir d’un bien.

examples.text: La possession et l’exploitation du sol par indivis, rationnelle, juste, féconde, nécessaire même, tant que la société exploitante n’excède pas les limites d’une proche parenté, - père, mère, aïeul et aïeule, enfants, beaux-fils et belles-filles, domestiques, oncles et tantes ; - est aussi solide que la famille même.

Au moment où il se présenta, Alice, qui l’avait vu venir, entrait aussi dans la salle, où son père et ses trois assidus discutaient à grand fracas sur le parti qu’il y avait à prendre pour rentrer en possession du diamant volé.

Mais quand l’Église, profitant de l’effondrement de la puissance romaine et du désarroi provoqué à travers les Gaules par les invasions barbares, s’installa dans le pays sans que nul n’y prît garde, son premier soin fut de s’assurer de la possession des terres.

glosses: Rapport possessif ou analogue à la possession, exprimé par les adjectifs possessifs comme ma, les pronoms possessifs comme le mien, les adpositions comme de, les verbes comme avoir, etc.
Terres possédées par un État ou par un particulier.

examples.text: Dans ce but il demanda à la régence d’Ensisheim communication de l’engagement pris par les parties guerroyantes de respecter les possessions autrichiennes, ainsi que les villes impériales.
Probablement dans un temps assez rapproché, la Russie cédera ses possessions américaines au gouvernement des Etats-Unis.

glosses: Jouissance de certains plaisirs, de certaines choses qu’on a recherchées avec ardeur.

examples.text: La musique […] emplit tout d’une caresse nostalgique. Ici sur un tressautement appliqué de java, là, sur la houle passionnée et la lente possession de danses moins animales.
La possession diminue ordinairement le prix des choses qu’on a le plus désirées. La possession n’a fait qu’augmenter son amour.

glosses: État d’un homme qu’on dit possédé par le démon.

examples.text: La possession diffère de l’obsession en ce que, dans la possession, le démon est censé agir au-dedans, et que, dans l’obsession, il est censé agir au-dehors.

glosses: The quality of being obsessed.
An idea that engenders a compulsive or irrational preoccupation, or the preoccupation thereby engendered.
An activity or entity that inspires a compulsive and potentially unhealthy fixation, or the fixation thereby inspired.

examples.text: Editing Wikipedia started as a hobby, but it's turned into a complete obsession of mine.

glosses: Influence or control by evil spirits without possession.

examples.text: if an evil spirit counterfeits the presence of God, and comes upon the man as an influence only, it may be described as obsession; but when a footing is gained in him, it is "possession," because the obsessing spirits have gained access, and possess the ground they hold, up to the extent of the ground given.
They should see that a perception of their identification with the Victor of Calvary is absolutely necessary if they are to constantly and victoriously resist the obsession of evil spirits.

It is true, that by the workings of the law of attraction, and the susceptibility of mortals to the influence of spirit powers, mortals may become obsessed by the spirits of evil—that is evil spirits of men who once lived on earth—and this obsession may become so complete and powerful that the living mortal may lose all power to resist this influence of the evil spirits...
